what is python: Python is a general-purpose programming language known for readable syntax and a broad ecosystem.
Python is a popular language used for scripting, data work, automation, and many other tasks.
what is a variable: A variable is a name a program uses to refer to a value.
Think of a variable as a labeled place to keep a value while a program runs.
what is a function: A function is a reusable block of code that performs a task, often using inputs and returning a result.
Functions let you give a name to a piece of work so you can call it when needed.
what is a loop: A loop repeats a block of code while a condition holds or for each item in a sequence.
Loops help a program do repeated work without copying the same code many times.
what is a list in python: A Python list is an ordered collection of items, written with square brackets.
Lists store multiple values in order, such as numbers or strings.
what is a dictionary in python: A Python dictionary stores values under keys, like names mapped to phone numbers.
Dictionaries are key-value collections, typically written with braces.
what is a bug in code: A bug is a mistake or unexpected behavior in a program.
When software doesn't behave as intended, the cause is often called a bug.
how do i debug: Reproduce the issue, read the full error, inspect the relevant values, and change one thing at a time.
Start with the smallest failing case. Check assumptions and use print statements or a debugger to inspect state.
what is an api: An API is a defined way for software components to communicate with each other.
An API describes how one program can request information or actions from another.
what is json: JSON is a text format for structured data using objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null.
JSON is a common way to store or exchange structured data.
what is git: Git is a version-control system that records changes to files over time.
Git helps track code changes and collaborate on software projects.
what is a git branch: A branch is a separate line of work in Git, so changes can be developed without changing another branch immediately.
Branches let you work on a feature or fix independently before combining it with the main line.
what is a pull request: A pull request proposes changes from one branch to another so people can review and discuss them.
A pull request is a reviewable way to suggest merging a set of code changes.
what is github: GitHub is a platform for hosting Git repositories and collaborating on software.
GitHub provides tools for code hosting, reviews, issues, and project collaboration.
what is a readme: A README introduces a project and explains what it does and how to use it.

what is the terminal: A terminal is a text-based interface for running commands and interacting with your computer.

what is an ide: An IDE is an application that combines tools for writing, running, and debugging code.

what is a compiler: A compiler translates source code into another form, often machine code, before it runs.
A compiler processes a program so it can be executed or used by another system.
what is an algorithm: An algorithm is a defined sequence of steps for solving a problem.

what is recursion: Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself on smaller cases, with a stopping condition.
A recursive solution repeats by reducing the problem until it reaches a base case.
what is html: HTML describes the structure and content of a web page.

what is css: CSS controls the appearance and layout of web pages.

what is c plus plus: C++ is a general-purpose programming language often used where performance and low-level control matter.
